title: When the new bell went live, gyms without browser alerts saw their old alerts come back as new
what: The change that made the bell remember what each person has read marked old alerts as already read only if a browser alert had gone out for them. Alerts are only marked as gone out for gyms that turned browser alerts on, or that chose instant alerts. For every other gym, which is most gyms, the past week's news came back with a number on the bell as if nobody had seen it, and every old to-do the server could not prove was handled came back as waiting, even though the owner had already seen and cleared them in the old bell.
expected: Everything that existed before the change starts as read for everyone, whether or not the gym ever turned on browser alerts.
who: gym owners and staff of gyms that never turned on browser alerts
how_often: once, on the day the change went live
fix_line: Treat every alert made before the change as read by all, not only the ones a browser alert went out for

title: On an older member app, a member whose plan ended or who trains on a pass is told only 'Could not send' when asking a trainer
what: The server now refuses a trainer question from anyone without a running paid plan at the gym. The newer member app hides the button for them, but an older app still shows Ask a trainer, lets the member type the question, and then says only 'Could not send'. Nothing tells them why or that renewing or updating the app would help, so they may keep trying.
expected: An older app gets a refusal it can show in plain words, or the member is told the question needs a running gym plan.
who: members on an older app version whose plan ended or who train on a pass
fix_line: Tell members on older apps in plain words why the question could not be sent

title: Sign in with your phone number finds no gym for a member whose plan ended yesterday
what: Phone sign-in lists a member's gym only while a plan runs today or they train on a pass. A member whose plan ended a day or a week ago, for example one who got a new phone and wants to renew, proves their number, gives the right first name, and is told no gym knows it. They then have to find the gym's join code some other way, right when the gym most wants them back.
expected: A member whose plan ended recently still finds their own gym (same number and first name), so they can sign in and renew.
who: members between plans or returning after a short break
how_often: every time such a member signs in on a new phone
fix_line: Also list the gym for a member whose plan ended within a recent window, with the same number and first name check

items.reason: No function in 0063-0098 is dropped or renamed (only undo notes); new versions are added beside old ones (share3 beside share2, owner_alert_list beside owner_alerts, member_talk_send_to beside member_talk_send) so older phones and admin pages left open keep working, and old terms stay valid. 0098 fills done marks for existing alerts. Sideload vs Play, watch and phone versions: not in database files.

Trial end: no reminder for trial gyms (existing). Plan end: India-day counting, a missed night skips a reminder (existing). Gym paused: sign-in, booking, asking and reminders skip suspended gyms. Staff leaves: PT classes and trainer questions stay (existing). Member returns after a plan ends: not found by phone sign-in (new). Year end and leap day: months use India YYYY-MM and next-month date maths; year windows use 365 or 366 days; no fixed Feb date found. Owner changes phone: sign-in reads the current staff number; a number change could not be checked without a live write.

Long-time members (joined before 23 Oct) get their join day only from 0092, which is not live; messages without a recipient keep the old rule; the Plus lock default applies to all gyms at once by the owner's choice; 0098 backfills done marks for existing alerts.
The path for old members exists in code (0092) but is not switched on live.
Rule applied: existing members' path not live = existing finding reused.

A brand-new staff person sees the last 30 days of open to-dos and 7 days of news as unread, which really is new to them; a brand-new gym accepts the newest terms once. At the switch-over, gyms without browser alerts saw old alerts as new.
Rule applied: old alerts marked new for existing owners = finding.
